body:
THREE NEW PRS UP, ALL AWAITING VERDICT, ALL Build-in-progress with merge-hold-gate green and no holds. Plus one non-finding I chased and killed, recorded so you do not chase it too.

  #2071  9afba49841  [AI:codex] feat(coordination): route typed recusal holds (STORY-1397)
  #2069  592e187811  [AI:claude] fix(list): validate and honour --fields on every output format (BUG-1520)
  #2070  3a7e022bb7  [AI:claude] fix(cli): correct the queue-work sequential-drain concurrency claim

#2071 AND #2069 ARE FROM THE DRAIN AND I HAVE NOT READ EITHER. #2070 IS MINE AND I OWE YOU ITS CONTEXT, BECAUSE THE PR IS HALF OF WHAT WAS DISPATCHED.

WHAT #2070 SHIPPED (TASK-185): the `queue work --help` claim "concurrency is pinned to 1" was false — STORY-1091 built the concurrent scheduler on STORY-1041's `[drain] pipeline_depth`, and the batch drain is one-at-a-time BECAUSE THE DEFAULT DEPTH IS 1, not because the engine pins it. `default_pipeline_depth()` = 1, clamp max 3, and above 1 the pipelined path overlaps a later member's implementer/CI leg with an earlier member's wait, merges still serial.

AND THE LANE FOUND A SECOND FALSEHOOD I HAD NOT ASKED ABOUT: `--sequential` NEVER PINNED CONCURRENCY AT ALL. It requires a batch, prints a notice, and falls through to the same dispatch — so with `[drain] pipeline_depth = 2`, `--sequential` PIPELINES. The flag governs order and per-member-PR shape only. It fixed all four copies of the claim, including deleting a `SEQUENTIAL_DRAIN_CONCURRENCY` const whose whole purpose was asserting the false invariant, and added a test that renders the help through clap and fails if "pinned to 1" returns.

WHAT #2070 DID NOT SHIP, AND WHY I THINK THE REFUSAL WAS RIGHT (TASK-186): I asked for an `--heft` flag on `aida edit`. The lane refused and punted with evidence, and I have since REJECTED the spec. heft is not a field — it is DERIVED GRAPH CENTRALITY, 0 of 4287 store objects carry a `heft:` key, it is absent from the Requirement model, and STORY-632 records the operator-resolved fork verbatim: "Never stored in the spec YAML." AN `--heft` FLAG WOULD WRITE A VALUE `aida cache rebuild` SILENTLY DISCARDS. The triggering observation was a misreading — nothing was "filed at heft 2"; that is one inbound plus one outbound edge — and the real defect is the NAME: heft reads as SIZE, means CENTRALITY, and was filed twice on that misreading.

SO THE SUBJECT DELIBERATELY NAMES ONLY THE CONCURRENCY FIX and carries no trailer. The lane changed the subject I gave it because mine claimed heft editing shipped, which would have been false. I would rather you know that was a considered refusal than read it as a half-finished task.

THE NON-FINDING, so you do not spend a check on it: I noticed `.aida/review-verdicts/PR-207.json` and suspected a truncated "PR-2070" — a verdict written to a wrong path would have been a serious defect on a day we have already found two in that substrate. IT IS NOT. PR 207 is a real, long-merged PR. What the file DOES show is the BUG-1466 provenance gap in its pure form: verdict "Approved" with reviewed_sha, reviewed_branch, recorded_by and recorded_at ALL null. A verdict that cannot be tied to a commit, a reviewer or a time — which is the historical population BUG-1466 counts at 452 of 481.

#2068 is still Build-in-progress on your APPROVED at b0e382d282; it merges when that reports. #2067 reworked at 8af4a8e2ea (ignore-with-reasons, and the lane's symlink-versus-copy argument overturned my "expected" answer); #2066 reworked at bb84dc4c8d with the docs-only suppression now REPRODUCED from run 35664201628 rather than inspected.
subject: Three PRs up (#2069 #2070 #2071) — #2070 is half of what I dispatched, deliberately; TASK-186 was refused with evidence and I rejected it
